propositions: Core push delivery implements five CAS retry cycles plus exactly one conditional terminal push, with strict delivery raising catchable PushDeliveryError while best-effort remains the default for all existing callers.

Strict delivery is opt-in via keyword-only strict=False default, additive to the public Python API, and translated to process failure only at the private module adapter boundary without calling sys.exit or owning process streams.

All existing library, CLI, MCP, importer, and store-write callers (event append, batch append, NDJSON import, transition close, delete, compact, claim) preserve their legacy best-effort behavior and inherit only the corrected five-cycle plus exactly-one-final-push retry budget correction.

Stable reasons for strict delivery failures distinguish policy declines from transport failures and carry underlying git/config detail plus the unpushed-commit count, with no ticket event or BRIDGE_ALERT emission.

The push-only implementation in push_tickets_branch excludes dirty-tree staging and committing, owned by dependent workflows, preserving working-tree state and enabling independent rollback via keyword-only API default.

Retry convergence is deterministically testable using real temporary git repositories with five rejected in-loop pushes followed by exactly one successful terminal push, with no duplicate or premature terminal push on earlier success.
